transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’ve been worrying more than I’d like. Once it starts, I can’t really seem to shut it off, even when I’ve made lists and checked everything I can.
Do unwanted thoughts keep popping into your mind over and over, even when you try not to think about them?
Yes… I suppose they do. It’s mostly worry that keeps coming back. Even after I’ve made my lists and checked dates and done what I can, I can’t quite turn it off.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind against your wishes?
I’m not sure I’d call them intrusive exactly. They’re unwanted, yes, but it feels more like I get stuck on them than that they just appear out of nowhere.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yes… it does move around. It can be the exhibition schedule, then my daughter’s travel plans, then something like the gutters on the house. Small things start to feel like they could turn into something much bigger.
Did this worrying begin after a specific stressful event or major life change?
Yes… I think so. It’s been about seven months. It started not long after my friend died, when I was trying to keep our projects going.
Even when you try to set the worry aside, is it hard to control?
Yes. That’s really… why I came in. Once it starts, I can tell myself I’ve made the list, checked the dates, done what I can, but it doesn’t seem to switch off.
Is this worry getting in the way of your day-to-day life?

A little, yes. I still do the garden and I go to book club, but I’m not quite as prepared as I used to be. And with the exhibition planning, I’ve been… stepping back from some parts of it, because it just feels harder to manage.
Are your worries mostly about your friend’s death and what happened afterward?

Not mostly, no. It started around then, but now it wanders… the exhibition schedule, my daughter’s travel plans, little things at home like the gutters. Small things start feeling like they could turn into something much bigger.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Not most days, no. I get worn out by the worry, but I wouldn’t say I’m depressed most of the time.
Has this worrying been happening more days than not for at least six months?
Yes… I think so. It’s been about seven months now, since not long after my friend died and I was trying to keep our projects going.
Have you been feeling restless or on edge a lot of the time?
Yes… fairly often. Even at home I feel kind of wound up. I’ll tap my fingers on the phone or get up to straighten something, just because sitting still feels… uncomfortable.
Have you been having trouble sleeping because of the worry?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I wake up sometimes, but I don’t know that it’s because of worry. I haven’t paid close attention to it.
Do you often feel easily tired because of the worry?

Yes… I do get tired pretty easily. Even if I’ve slept, I can wake up feeling like I’ve already done half a day. Then just watering the garden or sorting papers for book club, I’ll need to sit down for a bit.
Have you been having trouble concentrating because of the worry?
I’m not sure. I mean… sometimes I lose my place a bit, but I can’t really say it’s because of worry. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern.
Have you been feeling muscle tension a lot of the time?

Yes… mostly in my shoulders and neck. By the evening they feel really tight, like I’ve been holding myself braced all day. I notice I’m clenching my jaw sometimes when I’m reading or planning the garden center things.
Would you say this worrying is causing you significant distress?

Yes… I suppose it is distressing. I still keep up with the garden and book club, but I’m not as prepared as I used to be. And with the exhibition planning, I’ve started saying no to some parts of it because it just feels harder to manage.
Do you feel your level of worry is out of proportion to what is actually going on in your life?

Yes… I think maybe it is, at times. My mind goes from the exhibition schedule to my daughter’s travel plans, then to something like the gutters on the house, and suddenly those small things feel like they could turn into much bigger problems.
After your friend died and those projects were settled, did the worrying continue?
Yes… it did. It’s been about seven months now, I think—since not long after my friend died and I was trying to keep our projects going.
Do you feel the worrying is still closely tied to your friend’s death?

Not exactly… I mean, it may have started around then, but now it just seems to drift. I’ll worry about the exhibition schedule, then my daughter traveling, then whether the gutters need fixing. Small things start feeling like they could turn into something much bigger.
Before your friend died, were you already someone who tended to worry a lot about different things?

I suppose I’ve always worried some, but not quite like this. Lately my mind just keeps moving from one thing to another—the exhibition schedule, my daughter traveling, the gutters—and then they start to feel bigger than they probably are.
